# Shared local library engine v1 (implementation contract)

One canonical Paddock-format SQLite file, opened independently by both applications. No HTTP, pairing, running Paddock process, Review queue or Dealership requirement. Network integrations retain their existing contracts.

Source entry: `packages/shared-library/index.cjs`. Reproducible vendored entry: `vendor/slotforge-library/index.cjs`. CommonJS, Node/Electron with `node:sqlite`; async methods run in an engine worker. Both applications must ship the same engine artifact/version. Do not import its internal Store modules from the client.

`await open({application, installationId, sharedRoot?, legacyPaddockPath?, legacyProfiles?, thumbnailEncoder?})` returns a handle. `sharedRoot` overrides the per-user registration directory for isolated tests, not the application install directory. The resolver keeps the first established library location and refuses a missing/corrupt registered file rather than silently creating an empty replacement. `legacyPaddockPath` can identify an existing Paddock JSON/SQLite collection. Legacy Timing conversion is supplied by Timing's bundled read-only adapter. First adoption preserves originals and never matches physical cars by name.

All write inputs include `databaseId`, `recoveryId`, and a persistent `operationId`. Obtain identity once from status when creating an operation; persist it with retries. Never replace an old recovery identifier automatically. The engine attaches its handle's `installationId` as the editor/source of car operations. All methods return promises.

## Shared previews and compact catalogue (additive extension)

`thumbnail({carId, token?, expectedHash?})` returns a PNG data URL or `null` for a car without a main photo. Missing cars reject with `CAR_NOT_FOUND`. An optional catalogue snapshot token rejects stale reads with `QUERY_CHANGED`; callers must also recheck their snapshot and discard outdated replies before binding images after asynchronous encoding. `expectedHash`, when supplied, must be the 64-character lowercase SHA-256 of the original photo data URL. A mismatching photo returns `null` without generating a derivative. This additive guard lets immutable image URLs refer to precisely one photo, even if the car changes during loading. Existing calls without it remain supported. Original detail/media methods keep their existing full-resolution results.

Pass `thumbnailEncoder: async originalDataUrl => pngDataUrl` to `open()` to generate missing derivatives. Decode and resize in a browser worker, never the UI, main process or SQLite worker. The encoder must preserve alpha and proportions, never enlarge, and produce PNG at most 512 pixels per side and 2 MiB encoded. These are the existing Timing `png-512-v1` format and hash rules, not a new format. Cached reads work without an encoder; uncached reads without one reject and release their lease. Encoder errors do not roll back an already successful car save. Shared `carWrite`/`adoptCar` schedule bounded warming.

Paddock binds its opaque small-preview URLs to trusted lazy-asset file/car/hash metadata. Only the active canonical collection's main photos use this shared cache; full-size views keep original media, and other photos retain the private preview path. Committed write sets supply at most 32 photo-bearing car IDs for background warming, including background command and Portal saves. This does not scan the collection or delay save acknowledgement. Foreground requests take precedence over queued background warming. A cache failure falls back to the exact original photo's private preview. Reload/crash resets pending renderer jobs; only the current owning main frame may supply encoder replies. No network API or permission changes are involved.

The cache is `<resolved shared root>/thumbnails/png-512-v1/cache.sqlite`. Keys are SHA-256 hashes of the original data-URL string (the existing lazy-asset hash). No car record, canonical revision, change cursor, history or receipt changes when previews are generated. Photo replacement/removal selects a new hash/no preview. Backups may omit the cache; restored content selects derivatives by its own hash. Corrupt derivative rows regenerate; a structurally damaged cache rejects preview requests without repairing or modifying the canonical database. Cache eviction, gallery derivatives and LAN endpoints are outside this extension.

One generation lease per content hash lasts 60 seconds across processes. A later owner cannot be overwritten by a stale encoder. Requests coalesce per handle and encode serially. There are at most 128 pending explicit thumbnail requests per handle; warming stops admitting work at 32. Encoders time out after 20 seconds. Closing a handle cancels its thumbnail waits/encoding, releases owned leases where storage remains available, and drains accepted ordinary requests before closing the worker. A late encoder reply cannot store a result after cancellation. Physical host worker cancellation remains the host application's responsibility.

Requests made on a closed handle reject with `LIBRARY_CLOSED`; this is not the `null` result for a car without a photo. Paddock discards a stopped preview worker and opens a fresh handle on the next request, retaining its private-preview fallback for the interrupted request. An abrupt process death can leave a lease until its normal 60-second expiry; another process then regenerates it without editing the collection.

Ordinary worker traffic permits eight outstanding messages plus 128 waiting messages per handle. Overflow rejects with `WORKER_BUSY`; it does not grant permission to retry writes with new identities. Existing operation IDs and receipt/recovery rules remain mandatory.

`catalogueOverview({limit, offset?, search?, token?})` returns `{cars, definitions, total, nextOffset, token}`. Limit is 1–48; nonzero offsets require the prior token. It lists active cars in name order. Each row contains the normal editable projection plus `binding` (this installation's effective Timing settings), `original` (compact original companion fields), `custom`, `service` (the existing service counters), `hasPicture` and `galleryCount`. Main photos and original `extraPictures` are omitted. Original companion evidence is integrity-checked; cached summaries remain bounded to 128 entries/4 MiB, with a 1 MiB entry ceiling. Existing `catalogue`, `car`, settings, merge, history and network contracts remain unchanged.

| Method | Input and result |
| --- | --- |
| `status()` | `{engineVersion, databaseId, recoveryId, revision, file, changeCursor, capabilities}` |
| `backup({databaseId,recoveryId,revision,destination})` | Worker-owned, complete portable snapshot including Paddock inventory/documents/private data and Timing original companions. Destination must be an absolute, new `.sfpbackup` path; existing files are never replaced. Returns `{path,format,version,databaseId,recoveryId,revision}` for the captured snapshot. Identity/revision and recovery generation are checked inside the export transaction; no partial destination is promoted. Bundle it with Timing's private settings/live recovery data. This is not permission to restore only a Timing catalogue into the shared file. |
| `restore({databaseId,recoveryId,revision,operationId,source})` | Explicitly confirmed whole-library restore from an absolute portable-backup path. Never use for background refresh or Timing-only restore. Stages and validates the full snapshot, saves a complete recovery backup of the current library, commits with revision checks, rotates recovery identity and updates registration. Returns `{status:'restored',operationId,databaseId,recoveryId,revision,sourceDigest,recoveryBackup,duplicate,reopenRequired:true}`. Persist the exact input before calling; a lost response can retry that same input/operation ID without reapplying the backup. A marker committed with the restored records identifies retries. Reopen the library and quarantine all old-generation pending operations. A later restore supersedes the marker; older requests then fail their identity/revision checks rather than restoring again. |
| `bootstrapInfo()` | The original open result `{version,file,databaseId,root,adoption:[...]}`. Each adoption receipt includes `originKey,sourceId,databaseId,recoveryId,cars,sessions,originalOnly,originalBackup`. Use its original source ID even if Timing later generated a private source ID. A receipt from before a deliberate reset/restore is not permission to resurrect its old records. |
| `catalogue({offset=0,limit=50,search='',sort='name',archived=false,token?})` | `{cars,total,nextOffset,token}`. Cars are editable projections (`id,revision,archived,fields,unparsed,truncated`); photo not hydrated. Token required for consistent continuation. |
| `carSchema()` | Existing shared-car schema with field types, units, limits and current database/recovery identity. |
| `car(id,{includeMedia=false})` | Editable projection plus database/recovery identity; optional original `picture` data URI and `photos` array. Catalogue projections include `hasPicture` and `galleryCount` without loading photo bytes. |
| `profile({carId,includePicture=false})` | Existing signed Timing configuration/profile, captured from the current car. Never substitute this for missing historical configuration. |
| `carWrite(input)` | Existing shared-car create/patch/archive/restore fields (`action,carId?,expectedRevision?,set?,clear?`) and write identity above. Optional `timingExtras:{sourceId,originalId,expectedRevision,rawOriginal}` commits the Timing companion and original alias atomically with the car. Prefer `patch` instead of `rawOriginal` for ordinary edits: a top-level object of changed non-media Timing fields, at most 128 KiB. They are mutually exclusive. Unchanged compressed originals/media stay intact in SQLite. `expectedRevision=0` creates a companion; otherwise use its returned revision. Any conflict rolls back the whole command. Receipt includes `timingExtras:{sourceId,originalId,revision,hash}` when supplied. |
| `historyWrite(input)` | Existing guarded shared-history operation shape, including `sourceId,sessionId,action,expected,bundle,reason,editor`. Trusted local historical adoption is supported separately from network review. Optional `rawOriginal` is retained atomically as an engine companion. |
| `historyRead({kind,sourceId?,sessionId?,carId?,participantId?,offset?,limit?,token?})` | `kind`: sessions, detail, laps, statistics. Reuses shared-history response schemas. Unknown historical configuration stays null. |
| `originalHistoryWrite(input)` | Write identity plus `sourceId,originalId,sessionId,action,expectedRevision,reason`. Actions: create/replace/withdraw/restore. Create/replace also require `rawOriginal:{session,laps}`, `carIds` and `projectionReason`; preserve all original fields, including unknown fields. A null session preserves orphan laps. The original session ID cannot change. Withdraw/restore must omit rawOriginal and retain the previous exact body. Receipt: `{version,databaseId,recoveryId,sourceId,originalId,sessionId,operationId,action,requestHash,status:'committed',accepted:{revision,state,contentHash},originalOnly:true,duplicate}`. This is exclusively for unsupported original-only sessions; accepted rich history must use historyWrite. Existing adopted originals start at revision 1, active. |
| `originalHistory({kind='sessions',sourceId?,originalId?,carId?,state='active',offset=0,limit?,token?})` | Local-only access to preserved original history. Sessions returns `{databaseId,recoveryId,token,rows,total,offset,nextOffset}`; rows include source/original/session IDs, name, projectionReason, carIds, lapCount, originalOnly, revision/state/contentHash. State may be active/withdrawn/all. Detail requires sourceId+originalId and returns that metadata plus the original `session` object and lapCount. Laps returns bounded exact original `rows` plus total/offset/nextOffset; maximum 200, default 200 (sessions default 50). Continue with token; restart on QUERY_CHANGED. These sessions do not contribute measured records or mileage. |
| `changes({after,kind='cars'})` | Existing scalable change response; `after` is the opaque `changeCursor`, kinds cars/results. Bounded, with reset indication. No payload polling while idle is necessary beyond lightweight status checks. |
| `receipt({operationId,databaseId,recoveryId})` | Exact durable result or OPERATION_NOT_FOUND. |
| `adoptCar(input)` | Write identity plus `originalId,sourceId,data,rawOriginal,existingCarId?`. `data` uses Paddock car fields, including picture. Explicit established IDs may be linked; never overwrite existing car fields. Returns `{carId,originalId,sourceId,...}`. Original keys and raw source data retained atomically. |
| `adoptSession(input)` | Write identity plus `originalId,sourceId,sessionId,bundle,rawOriginal,reason?`. Existing accepted session identity is preserved; absent sessions are created with original evidence. No Review. For unsupported original formats use `bundle:null,projectionReason,carIds`; their exact originals remain available without invented statistics. Returns accepted identity and original source association. |
| `adoptionStatus({sourceId,entity?,offset=0,limit=100,token?})` | Durable original-to-canonical mappings and progress. Optional entity is car/session. Returns rows,total,nextOffset,token. Continuation requires the original token; restart on QUERY_CHANGED. |
| `origin({sourceId,originalId,entity='car'})` | Targeted original-to-canonical alias, or null. No collection download. |
| `extensionRead({namespace,sourceId,originalId,selectedFields?,omitMedia?})` | Preserved companion data plus hash/revision; namespaces `timing.carExtras`, `timing.historyOriginals`. Optional selectedFields or omitMedia produce `complete:false`; never write that projection back as a complete rawOriginal. Use a patch. Default complete:true retains every field. |
| `extensionWrite(input)` | Same key, write identity, expectedRevision and rawOriginal; isolated app-specific fields, never overwrite canonical car/history fields through extensions. |
| `close()` | Drain admitted operations and stop this handle's worker. Other application's access remains available. |

The engine refreshes its SQLite baseline before each call. SQLite transactions serialize commits; a competing writer triggers bounded retry using unchanged operation identity, followed by domain revision checks. Conflicting edits return errors and do not overwrite newer data. Both apps must observe change cursors and refresh normal screens automatically.

Whole-library restore is not automatically retried against a newer revision. `REVISION_CONFLICT` means re-present the action against the current library; `RECOVERY_CHANGED` means retain and reconcile old intentions, never replace their epoch. `RESTORE_UNCERTAIN`/`WRITE_UNCERTAIN` means retain the exact operation and retry it, not create another operation. A coordination transaction remains held through restore/registration publication, allowing recovery even if only an engine worker dies while its parent app stays open. Restoring another collection invalidates old peer handles with `DATABASE_MISMATCH`. Adoption receipts in the registration directory are retained, so old private Timing files cannot silently resurrect deleted data after restore.

For direct-file `carWrite` only, a `patch` may omit canonical changes (`set:{},clear:[]`) when `timingExtras` is supplied. The car must still exist, match `expectedRevision`, be unarchived and not be a rebuilt predecessor. The companion revision must match independently. The canonical car fields and revision remain unchanged; the companion revision and library revision advance together with the alias and durable receipt. Clients must observe the library status revision to refresh companion-only edits; the public car-change feed does not advertise a canonical change for them. Empty patches without a companion remain invalid. The older service/HTTP write contract is unchanged.

### Shared custom fields and service counters

`customSchema()` returns `{databaseId,recoveryId,revision,definitions}`. Definitions retain `{id,revision,label,type,group,options}`; types are text, number, date, choice, yesno, notes. Adopted Timing definitions additionally retain `legacy:{sourceId,fieldId}`; list maps to choice. `customDefinitionWrite({...writeIdentity,fieldId?,expectedRevision,definition:{label,type,group?,options?}})` creates at revision 0 or edits the matching revision; changing an existing type is rejected. Omitted definitions and car values are preserved.

`customRead({carId})` returns `{databaseId,recoveryId,carId,revision,values,definitions}`. `carWrite` accepts optional `customValues:{set:{fieldId:value},clear:[fieldId]}` atomically with canonical fields and Timing companions. IDs must exist. Canonical custom values are strings (numeric/date fields validated); clear becomes empty text. An edit of custom values alone checks and advances the car revision. HTTP writes do not gain these fields.

`serviceRead({carId})` returns `{databaseId,recoveryId,carId,carRevision,service:{revision,lastServicedAt,servicesDone,lapsDriven,lapsSinceService,recordedLaps,includesOriginalOnly:true}}`. Service totals include saved physical lap records, including original-only tokens; they are **not measured performance or mileage**. `serviceWrite({...writeIdentity,carId,expectedCarRevision,expectedRevision,action:'initialize'|'set'|'reset',values?})` commits with a durable receipt and advances the car/service revisions. Values may contain lastServicedAt (ISO/null), servicesDone, lapsDriven, lapsSinceService (nonnegative integers). Initialize requires service revision 0. Reset uses the current time, sets lapsSinceService to 0, increments servicesDone, and adds a maintenance event. Stale/archived/rebuilt cars reject edits.

Automatic first adoption preserves legacy counters as baselines **after** adopting old history, so old laps are not added twice. Subsequent accepted-history and original-only corrections/withdrawals update the derived difference. Unknown historical dates stay unknown; their baseline contribution is recorded at reset. Totals clamp at zero rather than producing negative counters. Raw legacy counters remain in original evidence. A user-set counter becomes a new baseline at the current accepted evidence. Simulation interval/damage/tyre settings remain companions.

### Bounded Timing screen projections (response details)

`timingRead(input)` runs in the common worker against one SQLite snapshot. It never returns all lap arrays. `kind:'sessions'` aliases `historyRead({kind:'sessions',...})`; `kind:'session'` aliases the existing detail read. Other kinds return `{version,databaseId,recoveryId,token,...}`:

- `home`: `summary`, up to 20 `topDistanceCars`, up to 20 `recentSessions`, up to 20 `topWinners`, `fastestThisWeek` (one track-eligible lap or null), and `weekStart`. Supply `weekStart` as UTC ISO timestamp for the user's local week boundary; omitted means Monday 00:00 UTC. Top winners retain sourceId, driverId, driverName, wins and lastWinAt; each participating driver gets at most one overall finished win per session, including endurance co-drivers. Class awards and repeated laps/heats do not add overall wins. Team aggregation remains separate.
- `carStatistics`: requires `carId`; returns `summary` and `tracks:{rows,total,offset,nextOffset}`. Each track row retains `sourceId,trackId,trackName` and summary measurements. Use `from` for a known service timestamp; this is measured evidence, not the legacy manual service counter.
- `records`: `scope:'personal'|'track'` (default track), `rows,total,offset,nextOffset`. Track winners group by source/track/lane. Personal winners group by source/track/car/driver/lane. Rows include exact sourceId, sessionId, participantId, lapId, originLapId (null when not recorded), lapNumber, carId/carName, trackId/trackName, driverId/driverName, lane, durationMs, startedAt and endedAtMs. Ties resolve deterministically. `sort:'time'` orders winners by fastest duration first; default `track` groups their display order.
- `classes`: paged `{rows:[{label}],total,offset,nextOffset}` of distinct nonempty canonical raceClass labels. No pictures or full car records are loaded.

Filters: `carId,sourceId,trackId,driverId,lane,from,to`. Track/driver filters require sourceId. Dates are UTC ISO, from inclusive/to exclusive. Paged rows use offset and limit (1–100, default 50); continuation requires the first `token`. A changed library returns QUERY_CHANGED; restart the page. All counts exclude withdrawn, quarantined, virtual and original-only evidence. Record winners additionally require explicit validity, non-pit status, duration and their separate personal/track eligibility. Unknown distance remains unknown; classification never adds distance.

Summary fields: recordedLaps, acceptedSessions, historicalSessions, measuredLaps, validLaps, measuredTimeMs (sum of valid non-pit durations), averageLapMs, bestPersonalLapMs, bestTrackLapMs, personalRecordLaps, trackRecordLaps, distanceM, distanceLaps, unknownDistanceLaps, lastDrivenAt, overallWins, classWins, distanceComplete, originalOnlyIncluded:false, manualIncluded:false. Track/top-distance rows contain the measurement fields; wins are supplied on the summary only. A session contributes to these lap-based summaries only when it has retained physical lap evidence. Archived/deleted car identities remain attributable to recorded evidence.

Raw originals are compressed JSON assets in the same canonical file, referenced by independently stored companion records. Compression is divided into 1 MiB chunks to remain compatible with portable-backup asset limits. The current per-original JSON limit is 200 MiB; exceeding it fails explicitly and leaves the source intact. Originals are preserved by backup/restore; they are not independently editable copies of the catalogue.

Original-only history is a separate projection from accepted racing statistics, not a second database. `accepted.contentHash` on original-only receipts hashes the preserved original body; withdrawal/restore change state/revision while retaining that hash. Do not merge its totals into measured statistics. Normal live refresh should invalidate original-only pages when `status().revision` changes (or a local file notification fires); the public `changes(kind='results')` stream intentionally omits private original-only records. No HTTP endpoint or LAN permission is added for this data.

`open()` automatically discovers and adopts the old Timing profile under `appData` (optional override for tests). An active SQLite selection always takes precedence over stale JSON. It preserves a source backup, canonical pre-adoption backup, durable per-item aliases and a one-time completion receipt. It never matches cars by name. Opening after a deliberate reset or restore does not re-import abandoned legacy files. If an older app is still changing its legacy file during adoption, startup stops explicitly rather than silently accepting an incomplete cutover. Both apps must ship the new engine before relying on shared writes.

The normal per-account registration lives under `%LOCALAPPDATA%/SlotForge/shared-library/v1` on Windows, `~/Library/Application Support/SlotForge/shared-library/v1` on macOS, and `$XDG_DATA_HOME/slotforge/shared-library/v1` (default `~/.local/share`) on Linux. Its `library.json` points to the one canonical SQLite file. An existing Paddock library keeps its established file path and database ID. Clients do not select another library simply because the registered file is unavailable.

Complete compatibility qualification must cover installation in either order, two processes, one process absent for weeks, interrupted adoption, conflicting writes and restore/retry safety before activation. Host database tests and a native Paddock test are passing; the full Timing application adapter and joint native tests remain separate work.

### Native Timing history projection, version 2

Native local adoption uses the bundled Timing reader's `project.session()` and retains the exact original session and laps. Missing false exclusion flags in native Timing rows follow Timing's saved-row semantics. Invalid, pit, late, red-flag and too-slow laps cannot gain record eligibility; personal and track exclusions remain independent. Unknown validity stays unknown. Only recorded historical lane lengths supply distance.

The engine recomputes the native bundle using its own source/car mappings and compares its hash before assigning the internal stored `nativeTiming:1` marker. Native corrections must target an adopted source/session, preserve the enclosing original session ID, supply the raw original and match its recomputed bundle. The marker is not a public payload option. Public Historical Review still rejects eligibility claims.

On opening either updated app, projection-v1 adopted sessions can be repaired from retained originals. Repair only applies to unchanged active revision-1 sessions in the original recovery generation, matching the adoption receipt and original hash. A backup is made first; repair is an atomic audited revision-2 replacement with a durable command receipt. Corrections, withdrawals, missing cars, changed originals and pre-restore adoptions are skipped. Car IDs, raw originals and service counters are unchanged. Reopening does not duplicate sessions or laps. Clients must refresh their accepted revision before subsequent edits; stale revision-1 writes conflict normally.

History list and Timing record/recent-session rows add `savedAt`, `effectiveDate` and `dateBasis` (`started`, `saved`, `unknown`). `startedAt` remains the actual recorded start or null. `effectiveDate` prefers start, then save date. Timing summaries use that date for `lastDrivenAt`, with `lastDrivenDateBasis`; date filters and chronological views in the direct engine use available dates. HTTP history endpoints retain start-date filtering by default; callers can explicitly select `dateBasis=available`. A saved date must be labelled as saved in the UI.

Both applications should use the same updated engine artifact. Existing network Historical Review and measured delivery retain their separate validation and approval rules.

Status: being implemented; this document is not a completion or activation claim.
